'''Georgia McClure Benkart''' (December 30, 1947 – April 29, 2022)<ref name="wiscobit">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-30 |title=In Memoriam: Georgia Benkart |url=https://math.wisc.edu/2022/04/30/in-memoriam-georgia-benkart/ |access-date=2022-05-02 |website=Department of Mathematics |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="census">{{Cite web |date=1950 |title=1950 Census |url=https://1950census.archives.gov/search/?county=Youngstown%2C%20Mahoning&name=Benkart&page=1&state=OH |access-date=2 May 2022 |website=United States Archives}}</ref><ref name="Code 1947">{{cite web | title=Georgia Benkart | website=OfficialUSA.com Records | date=1947-12-30 | url=https://www.officialusa.com/names/Georgia-Benkart/ | access-date=2022-05-02}}</ref> was an American mathematician who was known for her work in the structure and [[representation theory]] of [[Lie algebra]]s and related [[algebraic structure]]s.
She published over 130 journal articles<ref name="ohiostate" /><ref name="msribio" /> and co-authored three [[American Mathematical Society]] memoirs<ref name="Memoir2002">{{cite book|last1=Allison|first1=Bruce|last3=Gao|first3=Yun|last2=Benkart|first2=Georgia|title=Lie algebras graded by the root systems BC<sub>r</sub>, r&nbsp;≥&nbsp;2|date=2002|series=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society|volume=158|publisher=American Mathematical Society|mr=1902499|isbn=978-0-8218-2811-3}}</ref><ref name="Stability Memoir">{{cite book|last1=Benkart|first1=Georgia M.|last2=Britten|first2=Daniel|last3=Lemire|first3=Frank|title=Stability in Modules for Classical Lie Algebras: A Constructive Approach|date=May 1990|series=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society|volume=85|publisher=American Mathematical Society|location=Providence, R.I.|mr=2488391|isbn=978-0-8218-2492-4|url=https://www.ams.org/books/memo/year/1990/|accessdate=June 10, 2014}}</ref><ref name="Memoir2009">{{cite book|last1=Benkart|first1=Georgia|last2=Gregory|first2=Thomas|last3=Premet|first3=Alexander|title=The recognition theorem for graded Lie algebras in prime characteristic|date=2009|series=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society|volume=197|publisher=American Mathematical Society|isbn=978-0-8218-4226-3}}<!--|accessdate=27 May 2014--></ref> in four broad categories: [[modular Lie algebra]]s; [[combinatorics]] of [[Lie algebra representation]]s; [[graded algebra]]s and [[superalgebra]]s; and [[quantum group]]s and related structures.

==Education and career==
Benkart received her BS degree in mathematics summa cum laude from the [[Ohio State University]]<ref name="ohiostate">{{cite web|title=Georgia Benkart|url=https://math.osu.edu/advisory-board/georgia-benkart|website=Ohio State University Department of Mathematics|access-date=5 May 2022|archive-date=May 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220525095524/https://math.osu.edu/advisory-board/georgia-benkart|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 1970 and an MPhil in mathematics from  [[Yale University]] in 1973. She completed her doctoral work at Yale under [[Nathan Jacobson]]  and wrote a dissertation entitled ''Inner Ideals and the Structure of Lie Algebras.'' She was awarded a PhD in mathematics from the Yale University in 1974.<ref>{{cite web | title=Georgia Benkart | website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=7979 | ref={{sfnref | The Mathematics Genealogy Project}} | access-date=April 30, 2022}}</ref>

Upon completing her doctoral degree, Benkart began her long career at the [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison]], first as a MacDuffee Instructor and eventually as a E. B. Van Vleck Professor of Mathematics until she retired from teaching in 2006.<ref name="Women Mathematicians at Wisconsin">{{cite web|title=A Brief History of Women Mathematicians at Wisconsin |url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/history_women_mathematicians |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140529151009/https://www.math.wisc.edu/history_women_mathematicians |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 29, 2014 |publisher=University of Wisconsin Math Department |access-date=May 21, 2014 }}</ref>  

She held visiting positions at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], California, the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]], New Jersey, the [[Aspen Center for Physics]], and the [[University of Virginia]].<ref name="msribio">{{cite web|title=Personal Profile of Dr. Georgia M. Benkart|url=https://www.msri.org/people/2676|website=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|access-date=5 May 2022}}</ref> During her career, Benkart delivered over 350 invited talks including 3 plenary lectures at the Joint Mathematics Meetings and the [[Emmy Noether]] Lecture at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Seoul, South Korea in 2014.<ref name="ohiostate" />

==Personal life==
Benkart was born on December 30, 1947, in Youngstown, Ohio,<ref name="Code 1947" /> to George Benkart II and Florence K. Benkart.<ref name="census" /> Her father served in the [[United States Army Corps of Engineers|Army Corps of Engineers]] and her mother was a teacher in Youngstown's "ethnically rich south side."<ref name="ohioobit" /> 

Benkart died on April 29, 2022, aged 74, from undisclosed causes in [[Madison, Wisconsin]]. Her survivors included her sister, Paula Kaye Benkart.<ref name="wiscobit"/><ref name="ohioobit">{{cite web|title=Georgia Bankart, Youngstown, Ohio|url=https://www.wkbn.com/my-valley-tributes/fox-funeral-home/georgia-bankart-youngstown-ohio/|website=MyValleyTributes|date=May 4, 2022|access-date=May 5, 2022}}</ref>

==Research==
Benkart made a contribution to the classification of [[simple Lie algebra|simple]] modular Lie algebras. Her work with J. Marshall Osborn on toroidal rank-one Lie algebras<ref name="rank one Lie algebras">{{cite journal|last=Benkart|first=Georgia|author2=J. Marshall Osborn |title=Toral rank one Lie algebras|journal=Journal of Algebra|date=1988|volume=115|issue=1|pages=238–250|doi=10.1016/0021-8693(88)90293-1|doi-access=free}}</ref> became one of the building blocks of the classification.<ref name="Gems" /> The complete description of Hamiltonian Lie Algebras (with Gregory, Osborn, Strade, Wilson) can stand alone, and also has applications in the theory of [[pro-p group|pro-''p'' groups]].<ref name="Gems" />

In 2009, she published, jointly with Thomas Gregory and Alexander Premet,<ref name="Memoir2009"/> the first complete [[mathematical proof|proof]] of the recognition theorem for graded Lie algebras in [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristics]] at least&nbsp;5.<ref name=MR2488391>Review of ''The recognition theorem for graded Lie algebras in prime characteristic'' by Murray R. Bremner (2009); {{MR|2488391}}</ref>

In the early 1990s, Benkart and [[Efim Zelmanov]] started to work on classification of root-graded Lie algebras and intersection matrix algebras. The latter were introduced by [[Peter Slodowy]] in his work on singularities. Berman and Moody recognized that these algebras (generalizations of affine [[Kac–Moody algebra]]s) are universal root graded Lie algebras and classified them for simply laced [[root system]]s. Benkart and Zelmanov tackled the remaining cases involving the [[Freudenthal magic square]] and extended this square to exceptional [[Lie superalgebra]]s.<ref name="Gems" />

Later Benkart extended these results in two directions. In a series of papers with Alberto Elduque she developed the theory of root graded Lie superalgebras.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Martínez | first1=Consuelo | last2=Zelmanov | first2=Efim I. | title=Lie superalgebras graded by P ( n ) and Q ( n ) | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | volume=100 | issue=14 | date=2003-06-27 | issn=0027-8424 | doi=10.1073/pnas.0932706100 | pages=8130–8137| pmid=12832611 | pmc=166194 | bibcode=2003PNAS..100.8130M | doi-access=free }}</ref> In a second series of works with Bruce Allison, Arturo Pianzola, Erhard Neher, et al. she determined the universal central covers of these algebras.<ref>{{cite journal| last1=Benkart| first1=Georgia| last2=Neher| first2=Erhard| title=The centroid of extended affine and root graded Lie algebras| journal=J. Pure Appl. Algebra|volume=205|issue=1|date = 2006| pages=117–145| doi=10.1016/j.jpaa.2005.06.007|mr=2193194| s2cid=14256793| doi-access=free| arxiv=math/0502561}}</ref>

One of the pillars of the representation theory of [[quantum group]]s (and applications to combinatorics) is [[Masaki Kashiwara]]'s theory of [[crystal basis|crystal bases]]. These are highly invariant bases which are well suited for decompositions of tensor products. In a paper with Seok-Jin Kang and Kashiwara, Benkart extended the theory of crystal bases to quantum superalgebras.<ref name="Gems" /><ref name="CrystalBases">{{cite journal |last1=Benkart |first1=Georgia |last2=Kang |first2=Seok-Jin |last3=Kashiwara |first3=Masaki |title=Crystal bases for the quantum superalgebra U<sub>q</sub>(𝔤𝔩(m,n)). |journal=J. Amer. Math. Soc. |date=2000 |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=295–331 |doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-00-00321-0 |mr=1694051|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Benkart's work on [[noncommutative algebra]]s related to [[algebraic combinatorics]] became a basic tool in the construction of [[monoidal categories|tensor categories]].<ref name="Gems" />

==Service to the profession==
Benkart served on several editorial boards including the boards of the American Mathematical Society for Surveys and Monographs and Abstracts,<ref name="AMS Ed Boards">{{cite web|title=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs Editorial Committee Past Members|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mathsurv-past.html |publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=May 6, 2022}}</ref> ''Communications in Algebra'',<ref>{{cite journal |title=Editorial board |journal=Communications in Algebra |date=1 January 1987 |volume=15 |issue=6 |page=ebi |doi=10.1080/00927878708823457 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00927878708823457 |access-date=6 May 2022 |issn=0092-7872|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and the ''Journal of Algebra''.<ref name="Journal of Algebra Editorial Board">{{cite web|title=Georgia Benkart|url=https://www.maa.org/georgia-benkart|website=Mathematical Association of America|access-date=May 6, 2022|archive-date=May 6, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220506224258/https://www.maa.org/georgia-benkart|url-status=dead}}</ref> She served as the associate secretary of the American Mathematical Society for the Central Section from 2010 to 2020,<ref>{{cite web |title=American Mathematical Society Council {{!}} February 1, 2017 - January 31, 2018 |url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/council/member-council |access-date=6 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170204085756/https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/council/member-council |archive-date= February 4, 2017 |format=web.archive.org |quote=Professor Georgia Benkart Associate Secretary (Central Section) Term:  February 1, 2010 - January 31, 2020 University of Wisconsin, Madison}}</ref> and was a member of the governing council in 1995 and from 2010 to 2021.<ref name="AMS Council Members">{{cite web|title=Council Past Members|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/council-past.html |publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=May 6, 2022}}</ref> Benkart was active in the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM) over many years, served as chair of the membership portfolio and the nominating committee, and helped plan the first AWM Research Symposium, which was also a celebration of the 40th anniversary of AWM.<ref name="AWM">{{cite web|title=Committees|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|url=https://awm-math.org/about/committees/|access-date=May 6, 2022}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Benkart received a Woodrow Wilson Fellowship from the [[Woodrow Wilson National Fellowship Foundation]]. Her work at Wisconsin was recognized by a Romnes Fellowship in 1985, a Distinguished Teaching Award in 1987, and a WARF Mid-Career Faculty Research Award in 1996.<ref name="University of Wisconsin Honors and Awards">{{cite web|title=University of Wisconsin Honors and Awards|url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/oldhome/news/2001/awards.htm|publisher=University of Wisconsin|accessdate=May 23, 2014|archive-date=January 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121091755/https://www.math.wisc.edu/oldhome/news/2001/awards.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2008 the University of California Lie Groups and Lie Algebras meeting was held in Benkart's honor.  Her talks and lectures include two invited lectures at the Joint Mathematics Meetings<ref name="JMM AMS-MAA Invited Address">{{cite web|title=Joint Mathematics Meeting AMS-MAA Invited Address|url=http://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm/1889_program_wednesday.html#1889:BENKART|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=May 23, 2014}}</ref> and a plenary lecture at a meeting of the Canadian Mathematical Society.<ref name="CMS Plenary">{{cite web|title=2001 CMS Summer Meeting|url=https://cms.math.ca/Events/summer01/photos/CMSindex.html#plenary|website=Photos from the 2001 CMS Summer Meeting|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|accessdate=June 10, 2014}}</ref>

In 2000–2002 Benkart was named a Polya Lecturer<ref name="Polya Lectures">{{cite web|title=Pólya Lectures|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/lecture-awards/pólya-lecturers|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|accessdate=May 21, 2014}}</ref> by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].  
She was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS)<ref name="AMS Fellows">{{cite web|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=May 21, 2014}}</ref> in the inaugural class of 2013.

She was elected and served as president of the Association for Women in Mathematics from 2009 to 2011.<ref name="AWM President">{{cite journal|title=President's Report|journal=AWM Newsletter|date=March–April 2009|volume=39|issue=2|pages=1–5|access-date=27 May 2014|url=http://www.drivehq.com/file/df.aspx/isGallarytrue/shareID8755087/fileID929339010?1=1}}</ref> In 2014 she was selected to deliver the AWM-AMS [[Noether Lecture]].<ref name=NoetherList>{{cite web|title=List of Noether Lecturers|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/noether-lectures/|accessdate=January 26, 2019}}</ref>  The title of her talk was Walking on Graphs the Representation Theory Way.<ref name="Emmy Noether Lectures">{{cite web|title=Noether Lecture Profile|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/noether-lectures/noether-lectures-2014/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=January 26, 2019}}</ref>

In 2014 at the International Congress of Mathematicians held in Seoul, she delivered the ICM Emmy Noether Lecture.<ref name="ICM Emmy Noether Lecture">{{cite web|title=ICM Emmy Noether Lecture |url=http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/speciallectures |publisher=the organizing committee of Seoul ICM 2014 |accessdate=October 2, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006121521/http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/speciallectures |archivedate=October 6, 2014 }}</ref>

She was selected as a fellow of the Association for Women in Mathematics in the inaugural 2018 class.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=November 23, 2020}}</ref>

In 2022, a tribute to her contributions to her field, ''"Gems from the Work of Georgia Benkart"'', appeared in the ''Notices of the American Mathematical Society''.<ref name="Gems">{{cite journal|title=Gems from the Work of Georgia Benkart|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=March 2022|volume=69|issue=3|pages=375–384|accessdate=April 30, 2022|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202203/rnoti-p375.pdf}}</ref>

The [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Remembering Georgia Benkart (1947 - 2022)|website=American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7023|access-date=4 May 2022}}</ref> and the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] mathematics department<ref>{{cite web|title=Georgia Benkart Remembrances|website=University of Wisconsin – Madison Mathematics|url=https://math.wisc.edu/georgia-benkart-rememberances/|access-date=4 May 2022}}</ref> posted remembrances of Benkart.
